**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 26, verses 99–104:**

﴿Only the criminals led us astray﴾, that is, the possessors of crimes, great sins, and audacity, and they are their leaders, those of standing in the world and of having followers, as in their saying: ﴿We obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67]. Al-Suddi said: they are the first ones whom they followed. It was said: the criminals are the devils. It was said: those who called them to worship idols from among the jinn and mankind. Ibn Juraij said: Iblis and the son of Adam who killed (his brother), because he was the first to establish killing and various kinds of sins.

When they saw that the intercession of the angels, the prophets, and the scholars was beneficial for the people of faith, and the intercession of a close friend for his close friend in particular, they said, in a manner of regret and lament: ﴿So we have no intercessors, nor any sincere friend﴾. Ibn Juraij said: "intercessors" from (p-28) the angels, and "a friend" from among people. The word *shafi'* (intercessor) implies a high rank with the one interceded with, and the word *sadiq* (friend) implies intense participation and support; it is *fa'il* from *sadaqa al-wudd* (he was true in affection), one of the intensive patterns. The negation of intercessors and friend may be a negation of their existence at that time, although they exist for the believers, since the angels intercede and the believers are friends, as He said: "﴿The close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]." Or that is according to their belief concerning their deities, that they are their intercessors with God, and that they have friends among mankind and the devils. So by their negation they intended the negation of whatever benefit is connected to them, because what does not benefit has the ruling of the nonexistent. Thus the meaning becomes: "So we have no benefit from those whom we believed to be intercessors and friends." The intercessors were put in the plural because they are usually numerous. Do you not see that one intercedes for someone who has fallen into a predicament, even one he does not know? The friend was put in the singular because of its scarcity, yet it is intended in the plural sense, since it is said: "they are a friend (*sadiq*)," meaning friends, just as it is said: "they are an enemy (*ʿadu*)," meaning enemies.

The apparent view is that *law* here has taken on the meaning of wishing (*tamanni*), and *fa-nakuna* ("so that we would be") is the answer, as if it were said: "Would that we had a return, so that we would be [believers]." It was also said: it is the *khalisa* (the pure, i.e., the non-conditional, hypothetical use) for indicating what would have happened had something else occurred, so that His saying *fa-nakuna* is conjoined (*ma'tuf*, coordinated) to *karratan* ("a return"), meaning: "so that we would be among the believers." The answer of *law* is omitted, meaning: "we would have had intercessors and friends," or "we would have been delivered from the punishment."

The apparent view is that all these sentences are connected to the speech of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): he reported what God had informed him of the circumstances of the Day of Resurrection and what will happen therein to his people.

Ibn Attiyah said: these verses, from His saying "the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail," are in my view a separate statement from the speech of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and they are a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, connected to the description of that Day at which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood in his supplication that he not be disgraced therein. End of quotation. Ibn Attiyah had parsed "the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail" as an apposition (*badal*, substitution) for "the Day they are raised," but according to this, what he mentioned of separating the speech and making part of it the speech of Ibrahim and part of it the speech of God cannot be achieved, because the governing element in the apposition, according to the view of the majority (*al-jumhur*, the majority of grammarians), is another verb derived from the same root as the first, or the first itself. In both assumptions, it cannot be the speech of God, since the sense would become: "And do not disgrace me on the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail."

The reference in His saying "Indeed in that is a sign" is to the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his dialogue with his people. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾: that is, most of the people of Ibrahim. He, the Exalted, made clear that most of his people did not believe, despite the manifestation of these proofs with which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) argued. In this there is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding his people's denial of him.

The negation of intercessors and friend may be a negation of their existence at that time, although they exist for the believers, since the angels intercede and the believers are friends, as He said: "﴿The close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]." Or that is according to their belief concerning their deities, that they are their intercessors with God, and that they have friends among mankind and the devils. So by their negation they intended the negation of whatever benefit is connected to them, because what does not benefit has the ruling of the nonexistent. Thus the meaning becomes: "So we have no benefit from those whom we believed to be intercessors and friends." The intercessors were put in the plural because they are usually numerous. Do you not see that one intercedes for someone who has fallen into a predicament, even one he does not know? The friend was put in the singular because of its scarcity, yet it is intended in the plural sense, since it is said: "they are a friend (*sadiq*)," meaning friends, just as it is said: "they are an enemy (*ʿadu*)," meaning enemies.

The apparent view is that *law* here has taken on the meaning of wishing (*tamanni*), and *fa-nakuna* ("so that we would be") is the answer, as if it were said: "Would that we had a return, so that we would be [believers]." It was also said: it is the *khalisa* (the pure, i.e., the non-conditional, hypothetical use) for indicating what would have happened had something else occurred, so that His saying *fa-nakuna* is conjoined (*ma'tuf*, coordinated) to *karratan* ("a return"), meaning: "so that we would be among the believers." The answer of *law* is omitted, meaning: "we would have had intercessors and friends," or "we would have been delivered from the punishment."

The apparent view is that all these sentences are connected to the speech of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): he reported what God had informed him of the circumstances of the Day of Resurrection and what will happen therein to his people.

Ibn Attiyah said: these verses, from His saying "the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail," are in my view a separate statement from the speech of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and they are a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, connected to the description of that Day at which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood in his supplication that he not be disgraced therein. End of quotation. Ibn Attiyah had parsed "the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail" as an apposition (*badal*, substitution) for "the Day they are raised," but according to this, what he mentioned of separating the speech and making part of it the speech of Ibrahim and part of it the speech of God cannot be achieved, because the governing element in the apposition, according to the view of the majority (*al-jumhur*, the majority of grammarians), is another verb derived from the same root as the first, or the first itself. In both assumptions, it cannot be the speech of God, since the sense would become: "And do not disgrace me on the Day when neither wealth nor children will avail."

The reference in His saying "Indeed in that is a sign" is to the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his dialogue with his people. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾: that is, most of the people of Ibrahim. He, the Exalted, made clear that most of his people did not believe, despite the manifestation of these proofs with which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) argued. In this there is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding his people's denial of him.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 26, verses 105–115 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

﴿The people of ʿAd denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 124] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 125] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 126] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 127] ﴿Do you build a landmark on every high place, in vain?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 128] ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 129] ﴿And when you seize, you seize as tyrants.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 130] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 131] ﴿And be mindful of Him who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 132] ﴿He has provided you with livestock and children.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 133] ﴿And gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 134] ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 135] ﴿They said: It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 136] ﴿This is only the custom of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 137] ﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 138] ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 140]

﴿The people of Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 143] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 144] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 146] ﴿in gardens and springs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 147] ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 148] ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, skillfully?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 149] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 150] ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 151] ﴿who cause corruption in the land and do not reform.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 152] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 153] ﴿You are only a human like us; so bring a sign, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154] ﴿He said: This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seize you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 156] ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 158] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 159]

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 161] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 162] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 163] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 165] ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 166] ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 167] ﴿He said: Indeed I am among those who detest your deed.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 168] ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 169] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 170] ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 172] ﴿And We rained upon them a rain; evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 173] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 174] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 175]

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 176] ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 177] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 178] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 179] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 180] ﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181] ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 182] ﴿And do not diminish people's goods, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 183] ﴿And be mindful of Him who created you and the earlier generations.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 184] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 185] ﴿You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 186] ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 187] ﴿He said: My Lord knows best what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 188] ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 189] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 190] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 191]

﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 192] ﴿brought down by the trustworthy Spirit,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 193] ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 194] ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 195] ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 196] ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 197] ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 198] ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 199] ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the guilty.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 200] ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 201] ﴿so that it comes upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 202] ﴿Then they will say: Will we be given respite?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 203] ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 204] ﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 205] ﴿then what they were promised comes upon them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 206] ﴿what they were given to enjoy will not avail them?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 207] ﴿And We did not destroy any town except that it had warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 208] ﴿as a reminder; and We are never unjust.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 209] ﴿And the devils did not bring it down,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 210] ﴿nor is it befitting for them, nor are they able to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] ﴿Indeed they are removed from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] ﴿So do not invoke another god alongside God, lest you be among the punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213] ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214] ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 215] ﴿But if they disobey you, say: Indeed I am free of what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 216] ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 217] ﴿who sees you when you stand,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 218] ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 219] ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 220] ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 221] ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 222] ﴿They hearken eagerly, and most of them are liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 223] ﴿And the poets, the misguided follow them.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 224] ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 225] ﴿and that they say what they do not do?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 226] ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember God much, and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what final return they will be returned to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 227]

(p-٢٩) *al-Mashhun* (المَشْحُون): filled with what it should be, to the proper measure of what is carried. It is said: *shahanaha ʿalayhim khayalan wa rijalan* (he filled it for them with horsemen and men). *Al-Ri'* (الرِّيع), with a kasra or fatha on the *ra'*, is the plural of *ri'ah*, which means a raised place. Dhu al-Rummah said:

> *Tirāq al-khawāfī mushriqun fawqa ri'ah*
> *nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yataraqraq*
> (Wings fluttering, shining atop a high place, the dew of its night glistening on its feathers.)

Abu ʿUbaydah said: *al-Ri'* is the road. Ibn al-Musayyib ibn ʿIlss said, describing caravans:

(p-٣٠) > *Fī al-āli yakhfiduhā wa yarfaʿuhā* ∗∗∗ *ri'un yalūḥu ka-annahu saḥl*
> (In the mirage it lowers them and raises them, a road that gleams as if it were a sheet.)

*Al-Ṭalʿ* (الطَّلْع) is *al-kufrā*, which is the cluster of dates before it emerges from its sheath at the beginning of its growth. Al-Zamakhshari said: *al-ṭalʿah* is what emerges from the palm tree, like the blade of a sword within it. The *shamarikh* (clusters) of the *qinw*; *qinw* is the name for what emerges from the trunk, as it is with its stalk. *Al-Farahah* is the goodness of a thing's appearance, its strength, and its perfection in its kind. It is also said: wit and vigor. *Al-Qali* means the one who hates; *qalā yaqlī* and *yaqlā*. Its occurrence on the pattern *yafʿal* with a fatha on the ʿayn is anomalous. *Al-Jibillah* (الجِبِلَّة) is the coarse, thick, embodied creation, derived from *al-jabal* (mountain). The poet said:

> *Wa al-mawtu aʿẓamu ḥādithin*
> *mimmā yamurru ʿalā al-jibillah*
> (Death is the greatest calamity that passes over the created multitude.)

It is also pronounced with a sukun on the *ba'*, and the *jim* may take three vowels. Al-Harawi said: *al-jabl*, *al-jibl* and *al-jubl* are dialect variants, meaning a very large crowd of people. End of quote. *Hama*: went off in his direction, said by al-Kisa'i. Abu ʿUbaydah said: he deviated from the course.

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

*Al-Qawm* (القَوْم) is feminine in a metaphorical sense; its diminutive is *quwaymah*. Therefore it says: ﴿The people of Noah denied﴾ (كَذَّبَتْ). Since its referent denotes individual rational males, the pronoun returns to it as it would to a rational masculine plural. It is also said: *qawm* is masculine, but was made feminine because it carries the meaning of *ummah* (community) and *jamaʿah* (group). The meaning of the denial of the messengers by the people of Noah was already discussed, even though the one sent to them was one person, as in His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ [al-Furqan: 37]. As for "brothers of Noah," it is said this refers to lineage, and it is said it refers to common kind, as in the saying "O brother of Tamim," meaning "O member of his community." The poet said:

> *Lā yasʾalūna akhāhum ḥīna yandubuhum*
> *fī al-nāʾibāti ʿalā mā qāla burhānā*
> (They do not ask their brother when he calls them to aid in calamities, about what Burhan said.)

The object of *al-taqwa* (mindfulness) is omitted. It is said the meaning is: "Will you not be mindful of God's punishment and retribution for your polytheism?" It is also said: "Will you not be mindful of violating God's command, so that you abandon your worship of idols?" *Amanatuhu* (his trustworthiness) is that he was known among his people for it, or that he was entrusted with delivering God's message. When he presented mindfulness of God to them gently by saying "Will you not be mindful?", he moved from presenting it to commanding it, saying: ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me﴾, concerning my advice to you and what I call you to, namely the oneness of God and worshipping Him alone.

﴿And I ask you no wage for it﴾, i.e., for my calling to God and commanding you to be mindful of Him. It is also said the pronoun in "for it" returns to the advice, or to the delivery, and the meaning is: I do not ask you for any of your wealth in return. He placed the command to be mindful of God before the command to obey Him, because mindfulness of God is the cause of obeying Noah, peace be upon him. Then he repeated the command to mindfulness and obedience, to emphasize it upon them and establish it in their souls, though the reasons differed: the first was made the effect of his trustworthiness, and the second the effect of not taking a wage. Then they did not look into the matter of his message, nor reflect upon what he commanded them, because of their disposition and upbringing in the love of leadership, which is what is stamped upon their hearts. So their nobles began to belittle his followers, and claimed that what prevented their belief in him was that the lowest people had followed him.

The first verse, ﴿واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾, is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah). The meaning is: "How can we believe when the lowliest among us have followed you, so that we would be equal to them in following you?" Quraysh did the same concerning ʿAmmar and Suhayb. The weak are more responsive than the leaders, because their minds are not filled with the ornaments of this world. So they are quicker to grasp the truth and more ready to accept it than the leaders.

The majority of readers recited واتَّبَعَكَ as a past-tense verb. ʿAbd Allah, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Aʿmash, Abu Haywa, al-Dahhak, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿd al-Ansari, Talha and Yaʿqub recited واتْباعُكَ as the plural of tabiʿ (follower), like ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb. It was also said that it is the plural of tabīʿ, like sharīf and ashrāf, and that it is the plural of tabaʿ, like baram and abrām. In this reading the waw is for the circumstantial clause. It was also said that it is conjoined to the pronoun in the phrase أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ, and this is allowed because of the separation by لَكَ. This was stated by Abu al-Fadl al-Razi, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abu al-Baqa. It is also reported from al-Yamani that it was read واتْباعِكَ with a genitive ending, conjoined to the pronoun in لَكَ. This is rare, but the Kufis (the grammarians of Kufa) allowed it on analogy.

الأرْذَلُونَ is in the nominative, as the subject of an implied predicate. It was said: "Those who believed in him were his sons, his wives, his relatives and the sons of his sons. On this view, رَذالة does not mean base trades." The discussion of رَذالة (baseness, lowliness) has already been given in Hud, in the verse ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27]. They intended by this to belittle Noah, peace be upon him, because they did not know that the weak among people are the followers of the messengers, as occurs in the hadith of Heraclius. This answer of theirs is extremely feeble, for he was sent to all creation, so the situation does not differ because of poverty or wealth, nor because of the nobility or baseness of one's trade.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears from the verse that the intention of Noah's people was to attribute vileness to the believers, by disparaging their actions, and not by looking at their crafts. This is shown by Noah's words ﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ and what follows, because the meaning of his speech is: my view and my knowledge of their deeds and beliefs are of no benefit. I am only satisfied with their outward state and content myself with it; then their reckoning is with God, the Exalted. This is similar to what the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'I have been commanded to fight people until they say there is no god but Allah,' the hadith in its entirety." End of quote. Al-Kirmani said: "I do not seek knowledge of what they have done; it is only incumbent upon me to call them." Al-Zamakhshari said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾, and what knowledge do I have, and what is the extent of my knowledge? The intended meaning is the negation of his knowledge of the sincerity of their deeds and of his awareness of their inner hearts. He only said this because they had attacked the lowliness of their faith, claiming that they had not believed through reflection and insight, but had believed through desire and superficial judgment, as God related of them in His words ﴿الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27], 'at first sight.' It is also possible that Noah rose above them, so that their words 'the lowliest' are interpreted as what is lowliness in his view: evil deeds and corrupt beliefs, and he does not regard what they consider lowliness. Then he built his answer upon this, saying: my only duty is to judge by outward appearances, without searching into their secrets or splitting open their hearts. If they have anything, God will call them to account and reward them. I am only a warner, not a reckoner, nor a rewarder. If you were aware of this, but you are ignorant, so you are carried along by ignorance wherever it drives you." The aim of this is to reject their belief and to deny that a believer should be called lowly, even if he is the poorest of people and of the lowest lineage, for the richness is the richness of religion, and the lineage is the lineage of piety." End of quote. This is an abundance of explanation.

Al-Hawfi said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ means 'what knowledge do I have of what I am engaged in,' and the preposition بِ is linked to عِلْمِي." End of quote. This construction requires supplying a predicate so that it becomes a full sentence.

Since they did not believe in the reckoning or the resurrection, he followed it with the words ﴿لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (if only you were aware), meaning that the Return is true and the reckoning is true. The majority read تَشْعُرُونَ with the second person (ta of address). al-Aʿraj, Abu Zurʿa and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani read it with the third person (ya of absence).

﴿وما أنا بِطارِدِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (And I am not one to drive away the believers). This indicates that they had asked him to do that, and he answered them with it, just as the leaders of Quraysh asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to drive away those weak ones who had believed. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿ولا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 52], "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord," and so on. That is: I do not drive them away from me in order to follow your desires or in hope of your faith. (﴿إنْ أنا إلّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: "I am only a clear warner," meaning that what I have brought is with the sound proof by which truth is distinguished from falsehood.) (p-32) When they made the excuse of not believing because of the faith of those beneath them, this showed that their hearts had not been opened to faith, since no one shuns following the truth when others share in it. So they began to threaten and warn.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 26, verses 105–115 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

﴿The people of ʿAd denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 124] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 125] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 126] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 127] ﴿Do you build a landmark on every high place, in vain?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 128] ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 129] ﴿And when you seize, you seize as tyrants.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 130] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 131] ﴿And be mindful of Him who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 132] ﴿He has provided you with livestock and children.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 133] ﴿And gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 134] ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 135] ﴿They said: It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 136] ﴿This is only the custom of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 137] ﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 138] ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 140]

﴿The people of Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 143] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 144] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 146] ﴿in gardens and springs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 147] ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 148] ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, skillfully?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 149] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 150] ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 151] ﴿who cause corruption in the land and do not reform.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 152] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 153] ﴿You are only a human like us; so bring a sign, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154] ﴿He said: This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seize you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 156] ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 158] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 159]

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 161] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 162] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 163] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 165] ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 166] ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 167] ﴿He said: Indeed I am among those who detest your deed.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 168] ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 169] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 170] ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 172] ﴿And We rained upon them a rain; evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 173] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 174] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 175]

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 176] ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 177] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 178] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 179] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 180] ﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181] ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 182] ﴿And do not diminish people's goods, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 183] ﴿And be mindful of Him who created you and the earlier generations.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 184] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 185] ﴿You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 186] ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 187] ﴿He said: My Lord knows best what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 188] ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 189] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 190] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 191]

﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 192] ﴿brought down by the trustworthy Spirit,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 193] ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 194] ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 195] ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 196] ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 197] ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 198] ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 199] ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the guilty.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 200] ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 201] ﴿so that it comes upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 202] ﴿Then they will say: Will we be given respite?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 203] ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 204] ﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 205] ﴿then what they were promised comes upon them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 206] ﴿what they were given to enjoy will not avail them?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 207] ﴿And We did not destroy any town except that it had warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 208] ﴿as a reminder; and We are never unjust.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 209] ﴿And the devils did not bring it down,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 210] ﴿nor is it befitting for them, nor are they able to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] ﴿Indeed they are removed from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] ﴿So do not invoke another god alongside God, lest you be among the punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213] ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214] ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 215] ﴿But if they disobey you, say: Indeed I am free of what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 216] ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 217] ﴿who sees you when you stand,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 218] ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 219] ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 220] ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 221] ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 222] ﴿They hearken eagerly, and most of them are liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 223] ﴿And the poets, the misguided follow them.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 224] ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 225] ﴿and that they say what they do not do?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 226] ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember God much, and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what final return they will be returned to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 227]

(p-٢٩) *al-Mashhun* (المَشْحُون): filled with what it should be, to the proper measure of what is carried. It is said: *shahanaha ʿalayhim khayalan wa rijalan* (he filled it for them with horsemen and men). *Al-Ri'* (الرِّيع), with a kasra or fatha on the *ra'*, is the plural of *ri'ah*, which means a raised place. Dhu al-Rummah said:

> *Tirāq al-khawāfī mushriqun fawqa ri'ah*
> *nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yataraqraq*
> (Wings fluttering, shining atop a high place, the dew of its night glistening on its feathers.)

Abu ʿUbaydah said: *al-Ri'* is the road. Ibn al-Musayyib ibn ʿIlss said, describing caravans:

(p-٣٠) > *Fī al-āli yakhfiduhā wa yarfaʿuhā* ∗∗∗ *ri'un yalūḥu ka-annahu saḥl*
> (In the mirage it lowers them and raises them, a road that gleams as if it were a sheet.)

*Al-Ṭalʿ* (الطَّلْع) is *al-kufrā*, which is the cluster of dates before it emerges from its sheath at the beginning of its growth. Al-Zamakhshari said: *al-ṭalʿah* is what emerges from the palm tree, like the blade of a sword within it. The *shamarikh* (clusters) of the *qinw*; *qinw* is the name for what emerges from the trunk, as it is with its stalk. *Al-Farahah* is the goodness of a thing's appearance, its strength, and its perfection in its kind. It is also said: wit and vigor. *Al-Qali* means the one who hates; *qalā yaqlī* and *yaqlā*. Its occurrence on the pattern *yafʿal* with a fatha on the ʿayn is anomalous. *Al-Jibillah* (الجِبِلَّة) is the coarse, thick, embodied creation, derived from *al-jabal* (mountain). The poet said:

> *Wa al-mawtu aʿẓamu ḥādithin*
> *mimmā yamurru ʿalā al-jibillah*
> (Death is the greatest calamity that passes over the created multitude.)

It is also pronounced with a sukun on the *ba'*, and the *jim* may take three vowels. Al-Harawi said: *al-jabl*, *al-jibl* and *al-jubl* are dialect variants, meaning a very large crowd of people. End of quote. *Hama*: went off in his direction, said by al-Kisa'i. Abu ʿUbaydah said: he deviated from the course.

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

*Al-Qawm* (القَوْم) is feminine in a metaphorical sense; its diminutive is *quwaymah*. Therefore it says: ﴿The people of Noah denied﴾ (كَذَّبَتْ). Since its referent denotes individual rational males, the pronoun returns to it as it would to a rational masculine plural. It is also said: *qawm* is masculine, but was made feminine because it carries the meaning of *ummah* (community) and *jamaʿah* (group). The meaning of the denial of the messengers by the people of Noah was already discussed, even though the one sent to them was one person, as in His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ [al-Furqan: 37]. As for "brothers of Noah," it is said this refers to lineage, and it is said it refers to common kind, as in the saying "O brother of Tamim," meaning "O member of his community." The poet said:

> *Lā yasʾalūna akhāhum ḥīna yandubuhum*
> *fī al-nāʾibāti ʿalā mā qāla burhānā*
> (They do not ask their brother when he calls them to aid in calamities, about what Burhan said.)

The object of *al-taqwa* (mindfulness) is omitted. It is said the meaning is: "Will you not be mindful of God's punishment and retribution for your polytheism?" It is also said: "Will you not be mindful of violating God's command, so that you abandon your worship of idols?" *Amanatuhu* (his trustworthiness) is that he was known among his people for it, or that he was entrusted with delivering God's message. When he presented mindfulness of God to them gently by saying "Will you not be mindful?", he moved from presenting it to commanding it, saying: ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me﴾, concerning my advice to you and what I call you to, namely the oneness of God and worshipping Him alone.

﴿And I ask you no wage for it﴾, i.e., for my calling to God and commanding you to be mindful of Him. It is also said the pronoun in "for it" returns to the advice, or to the delivery, and the meaning is: I do not ask you for any of your wealth in return. He placed the command to be mindful of God before the command to obey Him, because mindfulness of God is the cause of obeying Noah, peace be upon him. Then he repeated the command to mindfulness and obedience, to emphasize it upon them and establish it in their souls, though the reasons differed: the first was made the effect of his trustworthiness, and the second the effect of not taking a wage. Then they did not look into the matter of his message, nor reflect upon what he commanded them, because of their disposition and upbringing in the love of leadership, which is what is stamped upon their hearts. So their nobles began to belittle his followers, and claimed that what prevented their belief in him was that the lowest people had followed him.

The first verse, ﴿واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾, is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah). The meaning is: "How can we believe when the lowliest among us have followed you, so that we would be equal to them in following you?" Quraysh did the same concerning ʿAmmar and Suhayb. The weak are more responsive than the leaders, because their minds are not filled with the ornaments of this world. So they are quicker to grasp the truth and more ready to accept it than the leaders.

The majority of readers recited واتَّبَعَكَ as a past-tense verb. ʿAbd Allah, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Aʿmash, Abu Haywa, al-Dahhak, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿd al-Ansari, Talha and Yaʿqub recited واتْباعُكَ as the plural of tabiʿ (follower), like ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb. It was also said that it is the plural of tabīʿ, like sharīf and ashrāf, and that it is the plural of tabaʿ, like baram and abrām. In this reading the waw is for the circumstantial clause. It was also said that it is conjoined to the pronoun in the phrase أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ, and this is allowed because of the separation by لَكَ. This was stated by Abu al-Fadl al-Razi, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abu al-Baqa. It is also reported from al-Yamani that it was read واتْباعِكَ with a genitive ending, conjoined to the pronoun in لَكَ. This is rare, but the Kufis (the grammarians of Kufa) allowed it on analogy.

الأرْذَلُونَ is in the nominative, as the subject of an implied predicate. It was said: "Those who believed in him were his sons, his wives, his relatives and the sons of his sons. On this view, رَذالة does not mean base trades." The discussion of رَذالة (baseness, lowliness) has already been given in Hud, in the verse ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27]. They intended by this to belittle Noah, peace be upon him, because they did not know that the weak among people are the followers of the messengers, as occurs in the hadith of Heraclius. This answer of theirs is extremely feeble, for he was sent to all creation, so the situation does not differ because of poverty or wealth, nor because of the nobility or baseness of one's trade.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears from the verse that the intention of Noah's people was to attribute vileness to the believers, by disparaging their actions, and not by looking at their crafts. This is shown by Noah's words ﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ and what follows, because the meaning of his speech is: my view and my knowledge of their deeds and beliefs are of no benefit. I am only satisfied with their outward state and content myself with it; then their reckoning is with God, the Exalted. This is similar to what the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'I have been commanded to fight people until they say there is no god but Allah,' the hadith in its entirety." End of quote. Al-Kirmani said: "I do not seek knowledge of what they have done; it is only incumbent upon me to call them." Al-Zamakhshari said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾, and what knowledge do I have, and what is the extent of my knowledge? The intended meaning is the negation of his knowledge of the sincerity of their deeds and of his awareness of their inner hearts. He only said this because they had attacked the lowliness of their faith, claiming that they had not believed through reflection and insight, but had believed through desire and superficial judgment, as God related of them in His words ﴿الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27], 'at first sight.' It is also possible that Noah rose above them, so that their words 'the lowliest' are interpreted as what is lowliness in his view: evil deeds and corrupt beliefs, and he does not regard what they consider lowliness. Then he built his answer upon this, saying: my only duty is to judge by outward appearances, without searching into their secrets or splitting open their hearts. If they have anything, God will call them to account and reward them. I am only a warner, not a reckoner, nor a rewarder. If you were aware of this, but you are ignorant, so you are carried along by ignorance wherever it drives you." The aim of this is to reject their belief and to deny that a believer should be called lowly, even if he is the poorest of people and of the lowest lineage, for the richness is the richness of religion, and the lineage is the lineage of piety." End of quote. This is an abundance of explanation.

Al-Hawfi said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ means 'what knowledge do I have of what I am engaged in,' and the preposition بِ is linked to عِلْمِي." End of quote. This construction requires supplying a predicate so that it becomes a full sentence.

Since they did not believe in the reckoning or the resurrection, he followed it with the words ﴿لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (if only you were aware), meaning that the Return is true and the reckoning is true. The majority read تَشْعُرُونَ with the second person (ta of address). al-Aʿraj, Abu Zurʿa and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani read it with the third person (ya of absence).

﴿وما أنا بِطارِدِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (And I am not one to drive away the believers). This indicates that they had asked him to do that, and he answered them with it, just as the leaders of Quraysh asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to drive away those weak ones who had believed. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿ولا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 52], "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord," and so on. That is: I do not drive them away from me in order to follow your desires or in hope of your faith. (﴿إنْ أنا إلّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: "I am only a clear warner," meaning that what I have brought is with the sound proof by which truth is distinguished from falsehood.) (p-32) When they made the excuse of not believing because of the faith of those beneath them, this showed that their hearts had not been opened to faith, since no one shuns following the truth when others share in it. So they began to threaten and warn.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 26, verses 105–115 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

﴿The people of ʿAd denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 124] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 125] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 126] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 127] ﴿Do you build a landmark on every high place, in vain?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 128] ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 129] ﴿And when you seize, you seize as tyrants.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 130] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 131] ﴿And be mindful of Him who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 132] ﴿He has provided you with livestock and children.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 133] ﴿And gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 134] ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 135] ﴿They said: It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 136] ﴿This is only the custom of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 137] ﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 138] ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 140]

﴿The people of Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 143] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 144] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 146] ﴿in gardens and springs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 147] ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 148] ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, skillfully?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 149] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 150] ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 151] ﴿who cause corruption in the land and do not reform.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 152] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 153] ﴿You are only a human like us; so bring a sign, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154] ﴿He said: This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seize you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 156] ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 158] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 159]

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 161] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 162] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 163] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 165] ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 166] ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 167] ﴿He said: Indeed I am among those who detest your deed.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 168] ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 169] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 170] ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 172] ﴿And We rained upon them a rain; evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 173] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 174] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 175]

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 176] ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 177] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 178] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 179] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 180] ﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181] ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 182] ﴿And do not diminish people's goods, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 183] ﴿And be mindful of Him who created you and the earlier generations.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 184] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 185] ﴿You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 186] ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 187] ﴿He said: My Lord knows best what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 188] ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 189] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 190] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 191]

﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 192] ﴿brought down by the trustworthy Spirit,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 193] ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 194] ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 195] ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 196] ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 197] ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 198] ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 199] ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the guilty.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 200] ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 201] ﴿so that it comes upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 202] ﴿Then they will say: Will we be given respite?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 203] ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 204] ﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 205] ﴿then what they were promised comes upon them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 206] ﴿what they were given to enjoy will not avail them?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 207] ﴿And We did not destroy any town except that it had warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 208] ﴿as a reminder; and We are never unjust.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 209] ﴿And the devils did not bring it down,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 210] ﴿nor is it befitting for them, nor are they able to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] ﴿Indeed they are removed from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] ﴿So do not invoke another god alongside God, lest you be among the punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213] ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214] ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 215] ﴿But if they disobey you, say: Indeed I am free of what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 216] ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 217] ﴿who sees you when you stand,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 218] ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 219] ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 220] ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 221] ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 222] ﴿They hearken eagerly, and most of them are liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 223] ﴿And the poets, the misguided follow them.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 224] ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 225] ﴿and that they say what they do not do?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 226] ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember God much, and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what final return they will be returned to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 227]

(p-٢٩) *al-Mashhun* (المَشْحُون): filled with what it should be, to the proper measure of what is carried. It is said: *shahanaha ʿalayhim khayalan wa rijalan* (he filled it for them with horsemen and men). *Al-Ri'* (الرِّيع), with a kasra or fatha on the *ra'*, is the plural of *ri'ah*, which means a raised place. Dhu al-Rummah said:

> *Tirāq al-khawāfī mushriqun fawqa ri'ah*
> *nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yataraqraq*
> (Wings fluttering, shining atop a high place, the dew of its night glistening on its feathers.)

Abu ʿUbaydah said: *al-Ri'* is the road. Ibn al-Musayyib ibn ʿIlss said, describing caravans:

(p-٣٠) > *Fī al-āli yakhfiduhā wa yarfaʿuhā* ∗∗∗ *ri'un yalūḥu ka-annahu saḥl*
> (In the mirage it lowers them and raises them, a road that gleams as if it were a sheet.)

*Al-Ṭalʿ* (الطَّلْع) is *al-kufrā*, which is the cluster of dates before it emerges from its sheath at the beginning of its growth. Al-Zamakhshari said: *al-ṭalʿah* is what emerges from the palm tree, like the blade of a sword within it. The *shamarikh* (clusters) of the *qinw*; *qinw* is the name for what emerges from the trunk, as it is with its stalk. *Al-Farahah* is the goodness of a thing's appearance, its strength, and its perfection in its kind. It is also said: wit and vigor. *Al-Qali* means the one who hates; *qalā yaqlī* and *yaqlā*. Its occurrence on the pattern *yafʿal* with a fatha on the ʿayn is anomalous. *Al-Jibillah* (الجِبِلَّة) is the coarse, thick, embodied creation, derived from *al-jabal* (mountain). The poet said:

> *Wa al-mawtu aʿẓamu ḥādithin*
> *mimmā yamurru ʿalā al-jibillah*
> (Death is the greatest calamity that passes over the created multitude.)

It is also pronounced with a sukun on the *ba'*, and the *jim* may take three vowels. Al-Harawi said: *al-jabl*, *al-jibl* and *al-jubl* are dialect variants, meaning a very large crowd of people. End of quote. *Hama*: went off in his direction, said by al-Kisa'i. Abu ʿUbaydah said: he deviated from the course.

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

*Al-Qawm* (القَوْم) is feminine in a metaphorical sense; its diminutive is *quwaymah*. Therefore it says: ﴿The people of Noah denied﴾ (كَذَّبَتْ). Since its referent denotes individual rational males, the pronoun returns to it as it would to a rational masculine plural. It is also said: *qawm* is masculine, but was made feminine because it carries the meaning of *ummah* (community) and *jamaʿah* (group). The meaning of the denial of the messengers by the people of Noah was already discussed, even though the one sent to them was one person, as in His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ [al-Furqan: 37]. As for "brothers of Noah," it is said this refers to lineage, and it is said it refers to common kind, as in the saying "O brother of Tamim," meaning "O member of his community." The poet said:

> *Lā yasʾalūna akhāhum ḥīna yandubuhum*
> *fī al-nāʾibāti ʿalā mā qāla burhānā*
> (They do not ask their brother when he calls them to aid in calamities, about what Burhan said.)

The object of *al-taqwa* (mindfulness) is omitted. It is said the meaning is: "Will you not be mindful of God's punishment and retribution for your polytheism?" It is also said: "Will you not be mindful of violating God's command, so that you abandon your worship of idols?" *Amanatuhu* (his trustworthiness) is that he was known among his people for it, or that he was entrusted with delivering God's message. When he presented mindfulness of God to them gently by saying "Will you not be mindful?", he moved from presenting it to commanding it, saying: ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me﴾, concerning my advice to you and what I call you to, namely the oneness of God and worshipping Him alone.

﴿And I ask you no wage for it﴾, i.e., for my calling to God and commanding you to be mindful of Him. It is also said the pronoun in "for it" returns to the advice, or to the delivery, and the meaning is: I do not ask you for any of your wealth in return. He placed the command to be mindful of God before the command to obey Him, because mindfulness of God is the cause of obeying Noah, peace be upon him. Then he repeated the command to mindfulness and obedience, to emphasize it upon them and establish it in their souls, though the reasons differed: the first was made the effect of his trustworthiness, and the second the effect of not taking a wage. Then they did not look into the matter of his message, nor reflect upon what he commanded them, because of their disposition and upbringing in the love of leadership, which is what is stamped upon their hearts. So their nobles began to belittle his followers, and claimed that what prevented their belief in him was that the lowest people had followed him.

The first verse, ﴿واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾, is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah). The meaning is: "How can we believe when the lowliest among us have followed you, so that we would be equal to them in following you?" Quraysh did the same concerning ʿAmmar and Suhayb. The weak are more responsive than the leaders, because their minds are not filled with the ornaments of this world. So they are quicker to grasp the truth and more ready to accept it than the leaders.

The majority of readers recited واتَّبَعَكَ as a past-tense verb. ʿAbd Allah, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Aʿmash, Abu Haywa, al-Dahhak, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿd al-Ansari, Talha and Yaʿqub recited واتْباعُكَ as the plural of tabiʿ (follower), like ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb. It was also said that it is the plural of tabīʿ, like sharīf and ashrāf, and that it is the plural of tabaʿ, like baram and abrām. In this reading the waw is for the circumstantial clause. It was also said that it is conjoined to the pronoun in the phrase أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ, and this is allowed because of the separation by لَكَ. This was stated by Abu al-Fadl al-Razi, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abu al-Baqa. It is also reported from al-Yamani that it was read واتْباعِكَ with a genitive ending, conjoined to the pronoun in لَكَ. This is rare, but the Kufis (the grammarians of Kufa) allowed it on analogy.

الأرْذَلُونَ is in the nominative, as the subject of an implied predicate. It was said: "Those who believed in him were his sons, his wives, his relatives and the sons of his sons. On this view, رَذالة does not mean base trades." The discussion of رَذالة (baseness, lowliness) has already been given in Hud, in the verse ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27]. They intended by this to belittle Noah, peace be upon him, because they did not know that the weak among people are the followers of the messengers, as occurs in the hadith of Heraclius. This answer of theirs is extremely feeble, for he was sent to all creation, so the situation does not differ because of poverty or wealth, nor because of the nobility or baseness of one's trade.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears from the verse that the intention of Noah's people was to attribute vileness to the believers, by disparaging their actions, and not by looking at their crafts. This is shown by Noah's words ﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ and what follows, because the meaning of his speech is: my view and my knowledge of their deeds and beliefs are of no benefit. I am only satisfied with their outward state and content myself with it; then their reckoning is with God, the Exalted. This is similar to what the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'I have been commanded to fight people until they say there is no god but Allah,' the hadith in its entirety." End of quote. Al-Kirmani said: "I do not seek knowledge of what they have done; it is only incumbent upon me to call them." Al-Zamakhshari said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾, and what knowledge do I have, and what is the extent of my knowledge? The intended meaning is the negation of his knowledge of the sincerity of their deeds and of his awareness of their inner hearts. He only said this because they had attacked the lowliness of their faith, claiming that they had not believed through reflection and insight, but had believed through desire and superficial judgment, as God related of them in His words ﴿الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hud: 27], 'at first sight.' It is also possible that Noah rose above them, so that their words 'the lowliest' are interpreted as what is lowliness in his view: evil deeds and corrupt beliefs, and he does not regard what they consider lowliness. Then he built his answer upon this, saying: my only duty is to judge by outward appearances, without searching into their secrets or splitting open their hearts. If they have anything, God will call them to account and reward them. I am only a warner, not a reckoner, nor a rewarder. If you were aware of this, but you are ignorant, so you are carried along by ignorance wherever it drives you." The aim of this is to reject their belief and to deny that a believer should be called lowly, even if he is the poorest of people and of the lowest lineage, for the richness is the richness of religion, and the lineage is the lineage of piety." End of quote. This is an abundance of explanation.

Al-Hawfi said: "﴿وما عِلْمِي﴾ means 'what knowledge do I have of what I am engaged in,' and the preposition بِ is linked to عِلْمِي." End of quote. This construction requires supplying a predicate so that it becomes a full sentence.

Since they did not believe in the reckoning or the resurrection, he followed it with the words ﴿لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (if only you were aware), meaning that the Return is true and the reckoning is true. The majority read تَشْعُرُونَ with the second person (ta of address). al-Aʿraj, Abu Zurʿa and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani read it with the third person (ya of absence).

﴿وما أنا بِطارِدِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (And I am not one to drive away the believers). This indicates that they had asked him to do that, and he answered them with it, just as the leaders of Quraysh asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to drive away those weak ones who had believed. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿ولا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 52], "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord," and so on. That is: I do not drive them away from me in order to follow your desires or in hope of your faith. (﴿إنْ أنا إلّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: "I am only a clear warner," meaning that what I have brought is with the sound proof by which truth is distinguished from falsehood.) (p-32) When they made the excuse of not believing because of the faith of those beneath them, this showed that their hearts had not been opened to faith, since no one shuns following the truth when others share in it. So they began to threaten and warn.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 26, verses 105–115 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ ﴿He said: And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ ﴿Their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.﴾ ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 116] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117] ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me among the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 118] ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119] ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 121] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 122]

﴿The people of ʿAd denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 124] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 125] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 126] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 127] ﴿Do you build a landmark on every high place, in vain?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 128] ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 129] ﴿And when you seize, you seize as tyrants.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 130] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 131] ﴿And be mindful of Him who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 132] ﴿He has provided you with livestock and children.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 133] ﴿And gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 134] ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 135] ﴿They said: It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 136] ﴿This is only the custom of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 137] ﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 138] ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 140]

﴿The people of Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 143] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 144] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 146] ﴿in gardens and springs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 147] ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 148] ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, skillfully?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 149] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 150] ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 151] ﴿who cause corruption in the land and do not reform.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 152] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 153] ﴿You are only a human like us; so bring a sign, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154] ﴿He said: This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seize you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 156] ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 158] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 159]

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 161] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 162] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 163] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 165] ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 166] ﴿They said: If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 167] ﴿He said: Indeed I am among those who detest your deed.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 168] ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 169] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 170] ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 172] ﴿And We rained upon them a rain; evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 173] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 174] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 175]

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 176] ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not be mindful of God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 177] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 178] ﴿So be mindful of God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 179] ﴿And I ask you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 180] ﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the cheaters.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181] ﴿And weigh with a true balance.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 182] ﴿And do not diminish people's goods, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 183] ﴿And be mindful of Him who created you and the earlier generations.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 184] ﴿They said: You are only one of the bewitched.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 185] ﴿You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 186] ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 187] ﴿He said: My Lord knows best what you do.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 188] ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a great day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 189] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 190] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 191]

﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 192] ﴿brought down by the trustworthy Spirit,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 193] ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 194] ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 195] ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the ancients.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 196] ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 197] ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 198] ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 199] ﴿Thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the guilty.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 200] ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 201] ﴿so that it comes upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 202] ﴿Then they will say: Will we be given respite?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 203] ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 204] ﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 205] ﴿then what they were promised comes upon them,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 206] ﴿what they were given to enjoy will not avail them?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 207] ﴿And We did not destroy any town except that it had warners,﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 208] ﴿as a reminder;
